key_insight: A Gaussian surface bump accelerates vortex-induced transition and three-dimensional breakdown while preserving the spatio-temporal wave front associated with nonmodal response.
engineering_relevance: Predicting transition under combined surface roughness and free-stream vortices requires accounting for rapid three-dimensional disturbance growth.
method: Solve the incompressible Navier–Stokes equations using 2D and 3D direct numerical simulations.
Model excitation with a convecting vortex of fixed strength and sign and roughness with a Gaussian bump.
Analyze instantaneous flow features, vorticity dynamics, and nonlinear receptivity.
evidence_signal: The simulations identify four stages: roughness-generated disturbances, spatio-temporal amplification, wave-front emergence with unsteady separation bubbles, and bubble merging into turbulent spots.
watch_item: The abstract reports no quantitative transition shifts, and findings for a single Gaussian bump and prescribed vortex should not be generalized to arbitrary roughness or inflow conditions.
paper_title: Direct Numerical Simulation of Vortex-Induced Instability Over a Semi-Infinite Flat Plate with Discrete Roughness
